facts.label: Entity and perimeter
facts.text: The registrant and reporting entity is Elanco Animal Health Incorporated and its subsidiaries, consolidated (10-K page:7; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:1). The company operates as a single reporting segment, so there is no segment profit measure other than consolidated net income (10-Q Q2 2026 page:24). The 10-K exhibit list names the roles in the debt: under the Credit Agreement dated 2020-08-01 as amended by Amendment No. 3 dated 2025-10-31, Elanco Animal Health Incorporated is borrower, Elanco US Inc. is co-borrower and Elanco Financing (Netherlands) B.V. is the Dutch borrower, with "subsidiary loan parties", JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent and U.S. and Canadian collateral agent, and Wilmington Trust, National Association as non-U.S. and non-Canadian collateral agent and security trustee (page:147). The 4.900 percent senior notes were issued by Elanco Animal Health Incorporated under an indenture with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas as trustee (page:146; page:111). The receivables facility is documented in a Receivables Loan Agreement among Elanco SPEAR LLC, Elanco US Inc., and the lenders and lender agents, with Coöperatieve Rabobank U.A., New York Branch named (page:146), and the receivables are pledged for it (page:110-111). The pack does not name the subsidiary loan parties, does not state whether the senior notes carry subsidiary guarantees, and does not list the collateral; the risk factors say only that a significant portion of assets is pledged under the credit facilities and call the notes "senior unsecured notes" (page:44). The issuer-versus-guarantor-versus-collateral map is therefore an unresolved gap, not a conclusion. The context names no borrower, parent or guarantor. The name in the context ("Inc") and the registrant name ("Incorporated") are the same entity.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable for a credit snapshot, with the limits stated below. Elanco Animal Health Incorporated reports one consolidated perimeter and one segment, so every figure is group level. Revenue was 4,715 in FY2025 and 2,739 in the six months to 2026-06-30, up from 2,434 a year earlier; the trailing twelve month figure is 5,020. Reported net income was a loss of 232 in FY2025 because the fourth quarter carried 202 of impairment and restructuring charges; the trailing twelve month reported result is still a loss of 199, while six-month 2026 net income is 111. Adjusted EBITDA, which management defines and the filed statements do not print, was 901 in FY2025 and is printed as 1,008 for the trailing twelve months at 2026-06-30 (1,009 when rebuilt from the components, a rounding difference). Reported EBITDA from the same reconciliation is 773 on a trailing basis, so the net add-backs are 236.

facts.label: Adjusted EBITDA bridge and quality
facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA starts from reported net income, adds net interest expense, income tax and depreciation and amortization to reach EBITDA, then adjusts for the cost of sales items, asset impairment, restructuring and other special charges, sold royalty revenue, the 2024 divestiture gain and other (income) expense items (Aug release page:14; Feb release page:18). For the trailing twelve months the adjustments are 252 of impairment, restructuring and other special charges, less 33 of sold royalty revenue, plus 16 of other expense items and 1 of cost of sales, in total 236, equal to 31 percent of reported EBITDA of 773 (calculation below). Three points matter for credit use. First, the sold royalty adjustment removes revenue that Elanco still books under GAAP but no longer receives in cash, because the XDEMVY royalties go to Blackstone through 2033-08-24 (Q2 10-Q page:17); removing it makes Adjusted EBITDA the more conservative measure on that item. Second, the special charges are not one-off in size or frequency: they were 127 in FY2023, 150 in FY2024, 237 in FY2025 and 252 trailing (10-K page:92; Q2 10-Q page:6). Third, the FY2025 charges include 155 of restructuring of which 116 is cash severance (Feb release page:3, page:5); the restructuring reserve stood at 124 at 2025-12-31 and 86 at 2026-06-30, with about 80 classified as current (Q2 10-Q page:11-12). That cash is spent after the add-back and does not appear in Adjusted EBITDA, though it is in operating cash flow.

facts.label: Rate and hedge exposure
facts.text: At 2026-06-30 floating-rate borrowings are the six term facilities (2,839) plus the securitization facility (100), 2,939 in total, against 750 of fixed-rate notes. Interest rate swaps of 2,300 notional convert floating to fixed and have scheduled maturities in August 2026; forward-starting swaps of 1,450 notional become effective in August 2026 with maturities between 2027 and 2031, up from 850 at 2025-12-31 (Q2 10-Q page:14). On the pack's figures the hedged floating debt falls from 2,300 to 1,450 after August 2026 and unhedged floating-rate borrowings rise from 639 to 1,489, before any hedging added after 2026-06-30, which the pack does not show. The company states that approximately 80 percent of borrowings were fixed or swapped at 2026-06-30 (page:12). The calculation below gives about 83 percent for the pre-August position and about 60 percent for the post-August position on the same base; the post-August figure is an analyst illustration, not a company statement. Net investment hedges (1,000 million CHF notional with tenors in 2026 and 2027, of which 200 million CHF was extended to 2031 in July 2026) generated 23 of interest income in six months 2026, recorded as a reduction of interest expense (page:13-14).

facts.label: Covenants
facts.text: Two financial maintenance covenants apply under the Revolving Credit Facility and, on consistent terms, the Euro Term Loan: a net total leverage ratio of pro forma net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA not to exceed 7.71 to 1.00 for the preceding four quarters, not subject to step-downs, and an interest coverage ratio of pro forma adjusted EBITDA to cash interest expense of no less than 2.00 to 1.00 (10-K page:109-110; Q3-25 10-Q page:15). The company states compliance with all covenants at 2026-06-30 (Q2 10-Q page:12). The achieved ratios are not supplied. Both covenant definitions differ from the metrics here: they use pro forma figures and covenant adjustments that the company says reduce its net leverage ratio below the printed measure (Aug release page:14), and a different net debt and cash interest definition. As an illustration only, not a covenant calculation: net debt of 3,159 divided by 7.71 is about 410, so trailing Adjusted EBITDA of 1,008 could fall by about 59 percent before the leverage test is reached on those proxies; and twice FY2025 cash interest of 206 is 412, so Adjusted EBITDA of 901 could fall by about 54 percent before the cover test is reached. The Senior Notes indenture has no financial maintenance covenant in the pack; it limits liens and sale-leasebacks and restricts mergers and sales of substantially all assets (10-K page:111). The Securitization Facility has covenants on the composition of the receivables portfolio, with compliance stated at 2025-12-31 (page:111).

facts.label: Liquidity by facility
facts.text: At 2026-06-30: cash and cash equivalents 530; revolver commitment 750, nothing drawn, unused capacity approximately 750; securitization facility drawn 100 with approximately 165 of undrawn capacity under a borrowing base (Q2 10-Q page:12, page:36). Total of these inputs is 1,445. No letters of credit or other usage of the revolver is printed in any source. The revolver matures in July 2029 and the securitization facility in June 2028, so no facility expires within twelve months of 2026-06-30. Known cash calls over the next twelve months that the pack supports: required amortization (63 for calendar 2026 and 63 for 2027 on the 2025-12-31 schedule), deferred AHV cash consideration of about 60 in January 2027, restructuring reserve payments (about 80 current), 2026 capital expenditure guided at 175 to 200 (10-K page:86), and interest. A fall in cash from 545 to 530 in six months came with 76 paid for the AHV acquisition, 89 of debt repayment and 35 of share withholding payments, against operating cash flow of 290.

facts.label: Cash flow quality
facts.text: Operating cash flow was 560 in FY2025 and 290 in six months 2026 against 233 a year earlier. Quarterly operating cash flow was 13 in Q1 2026 and 277 in Q2 2026 (May release page:4; Aug release page:4), which shows the first-half seasonal pattern; the company notes that parasiticide sales concentrate in the first half (Q2 10-Q page:30). Working capital absorbed 239 in six months 2026 against 185, with receivables up from 873 to 1,077 and inventories up from 1,737 to 1,769 since 2025-12-31 (page:6-7). Net purchases of property, equipment and software fell to 84 from 122 on timing of the Elwood, Kansas monoclonal antibody plant spend (page:37). Cash taxes of 225 in FY2025 compare with a tax expense of 8, driven by payments on the 2024 aqua divestiture gain (10-K page:84, page:126-127), so FY2025 free cash flow is a poor guide to a normal tax year; six-month 2026 cash taxes are not supplied. Interest on the liability for sale of future revenue and the sold royalties are non-cash and sit in operating cash flow adjustments (Q2 10-Q page:7).

facts.label: Latest quarter and after
facts.text: Q2 2026 revenue was 1,368, up 10 percent reported and 8 percent in organic constant currency, with Pet Health 718 and Farm Animal 633 (Q2 10-Q page:9; Aug release page:2). Gross margin was 58.3 percent against 57.5 percent (page:32). Net income was 54 and Adjusted EBITDA 288. The AHV International acquisition closed 2026-04-30 for total estimated consideration of 243, with 76 paid in cash and funded from cash on hand and a 50 draw on the securitization facility, repaid in the quarter (page:10, page:30). Net leverage as reported fell from 3.5x to 3.1x in the quarter (May release page:4; Aug release page:4). Management raised 2026 guidance to revenue of 5,090 to 5,140 and Adjusted EBITDA of 1,010 to 1,035 and targeted year-end net leverage of approximately 3.0x (Aug release page:1, page:4); these are management claims. Subsequent items in the 10-Q are the July 2026 extension of 200 million CHF of net investment hedges to 2031 (page:13) and legal: the Ninth Circuit affirmed the Tevra verdict on 2026-07-06 and denied rehearing on 2026-07-31 (page:22). No filing or release dated after 2026-08-05 is in the pack.

facts.text: This module opened the CP-0 handoff and used it as follows. It kept CP-0's finding that Adjusted EBITDA and net leverage come only from releases, and labels them as management measures throughout. It carried the covenant, guarantor and security gaps unchanged (see Gaps). It used FY2025 only for cash interest and cash taxes, as CP-0 advised, and derived Q3 2025 Adjusted EBITDA as 198 and labelled it derived. It refines one CP-0 statement: CP-0 recorded a difference of 2 between depreciation and amortization on the six-month 2026 cash flow statement (343) and in the EBITDA reconciliation (341) as not explained. The difference sits wholly in Q1 2026, where the cash flow statement shows 172 and the reconciliation 170 (Q1 10-Q page:7; May release page:14); Q2 2026 is 171 in both, because 343 less 172 is 171. The cause is still not given in the sources. The reconciliation figure is used inside the EBITDA bridge and the cash flow figure for cash analysis. CP-0 is otherwise not corrected.

facts.label: Definition risks
facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA differs from reported EBITDA by sold royalty revenue, restructuring and impairment charges, other expense items and, in FY2024, the divestiture gain. The company's net debt deducts the finance lease as well as cash, which lowers its net leverage by about 0.3x against this module's net basis (3.1x against 3.39x at 2026-06-30). Covenant EBITDA and net debt are defined in the credit agreement, which is not supplied, and are not the same as either. The cash interest figure is net of cash interest received on net investment hedges, which flatters cover relative to gross interest paid.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Elanco Animal Health Incorporated is a global animal health company selling pet health and farm animal products in more than 90 countries, with about 200 brands, as one reporting segment (10-K page:7-8; Q2 10-Q page:24, page:26). It was a Lilly business unit, became an independent company on 2018-09-18, completed separation from Lilly in March 2019 and bought Bayer Animal Health in August 2020 (10-K page:7). No sponsor, parent or controlling shareholder is evidenced in the pack, and the company says it does not anticipate paying dividends (10-K page:70). The creditor-relevant facts fall into three groups. First, the operating model is diversified by species and region but concentrated by channel and product: the largest customer was about 12 percent of FY2025 revenue and the top five product families about 38 percent, with seasonality in pet parasiticides that places most of Seresto and Advantage Family sales in the first half (10-K page:9, page:12-13). Second, the 2025 and 2026 transactions changed the capital structure: the October 2025 refinancing, the Blackstone sale of future royalties, the headquarters finance lease with a purchase option, and the AHV acquisition with deferred and contingent consideration. These are described in the Transaction summary and are priced in CP-1. Third, management is pursuing an innovation-led growth plan (Zenrelia, Credelio Quattro, Befrena) with a restructuring and a stated deleveraging path; those are management statements, and CP-1 shows that part of the improvement in leverage to date came from higher trailing Adjusted EBITDA rather than from repayment. Documented issuer behaviour is mainly supportive of creditors (debt repaid, no dividends, the AHV acquisition funded from cash on hand and a short-lived securitization draw), with two items that need monitoring: the use of a royalty monetization and a headquarters lease with a purchase option rather than debt, and management's statement that falling below 3x leverage will unlock capital allocation flexibility.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: No new debt issue, sponsor transaction or change of control appears in the evidence after 2025-12-31. The relevant transactions are as follows. On 2025-10-31 Elanco refinanced the Term Loan B due 2027, paying off a balance of 2,102, with three new facilities of aggregate gross proceeds of 2,106 (the Term Loan B due 2032 of 1,100, the Euro Term Loan due 2029 of 400 million euros and the Incremental Term Facility due 2032 of 540) plus cash on hand; issuance costs and discounts were about 32 and 20 was charged to interest expense for refinancing costs and deferred cost write-offs (10-K page:75, page:109). The documented purpose was to extend the debt maturity profile and lower cash interest, which is a supportive action for creditors. In May 2025 Elanco sold to Blackstone the rights to U.S. royalties and sales milestones on XDEMVY owed by Tarsus for 295, with net proceeds of 290 used to repay debt; the rights run for U.S. net sales from 2025-04-01 to 2033-08-24, Elanco keeps ex-U.S. royalties and later U.S. royalties, and the liability is carried at 315 at 2026-06-30 with an effective interest rate of 18.3 percent (10-K page:75-76; Q2 10-Q page:17). That cost of capital is high against the term loans priced at Term SOFR plus 1.75 to 2.25 percent, and the pack does not say whether the royalty rights were part of the lenders' collateral. In June 2025 Elanco started a five-year finance lease on its new Indianapolis headquarters, with a purchase option and a landlord put at 250 at the end of the term, which management expects to exercise (10-K page:76, page:121); a City of Indianapolis tax increment incentive totalling 64 funds part of the project (page:121). In June 2025 the securitization facility was amended to extend its maturity to June 2028 (page:111). On 2026-02-19 Elanco signed to buy AHV International B.V., a Netherlands farm animal health company (10-K page:138, a subsequent event to that report), and closed on 2026-04-30 for total estimated purchase consideration of 243: 76 cash paid at closing, 100 of deferred cash due through 2030 and a contingent consideration fair value of 67 for up to 140 of milestone payments through 2032 (Q2 10-Q page:10). The acquisition was funded from cash on hand and a 50 draw on the securitization facility, drawn on 2026-04-22 and repaid in the quarter (Q1 10-Q page:11; Q2 10-Q page:30). Management says the deal does not materially affect the deleveraging timeline (Q2 10-Q page:30), a management statement. In 2024 Elanco sold its aqua business to Merck Animal Health for 1,294 in cash, used mostly to repay term loan debt (10-K page:105). Financing documents for these transactions are not in the pack and are known only through the descriptions cited. The Q4 2025 rating upgrade is described only through the senior notes rate reset from 6.650 to 6.40 percent (10-K page:111; Q2 10-Q page:12).

The documented purpose was to extend the debt maturity profile and lower cash interest, which is a supportive action for creditors. In May 2025 Elanco sold to Blackstone the rights to U.S. royalties and sales milestones on XDEMVY owed by Tarsus for 295, with net proceeds of 290 used to repay debt; the rights run for U.S. net sales from 2025-04-01 to 2033-08-24, Elanco keeps ex-U.S. royalties and later U.S. royalties, and the liability is carried at 315 at 2026-06-30 with an effective interest rate of 18.3 percent (10-K page:75-76; Q2 10-Q page:17). That cost of capital is high against the term loans priced at Term SOFR plus 1.75 to 2.25 percent, and the pack does not say whether the royalty rights were part of the lenders' collateral. In June 2025 Elanco started a five-year finance lease on its new Indianapolis headquarters, with a purchase option and a landlord put at 250 at the end of the term, which management expects to exercise (10-K page:76, page:121); a City of Indianapolis tax increment incentive totalling 64 funds part of the project (page:121). In June 2025 the securitization facility was amended to extend its maturity to June 2028 (page:111). On 2026-02-19 Elanco signed to buy AHV International B.V., a Netherlands farm animal health company (10-K page:138, a subsequent event to that report), and closed on 2026-04-30 for total estimated purchase consideration of 243: 76 cash paid at closing, 100 of deferred cash due through 2030 and a contingent consideration fair value of 67 for up to 140 of milestone payments through 2032 (Q2 10-Q page:10). The acquisition was funded from cash on hand and a 50 draw on the securitization facility, drawn on 2026-04-22 and repaid in the quarter (Q1 10-Q page:11; Q2 10-Q page:30). Management says the deal does not materially affect the deleveraging timeline (Q2 10-Q page:30), a management statement. In 2024 Elanco sold its aqua business to Merck Animal Health for 1,294 in cash, used mostly to repay term loan debt (10-K page:105). Financing documents for these transactions are not in the pack and are known only through the descriptions cited. The Q4 2025 rating upgrade is described only through the senior notes rate reset from 6.650 to 6.40 percent (10-K page:111; Q2 10-Q page:12).

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: Revenue durability. Evidence: Pet Health volume growth in Q2 2026 was driven by new products Zenrelia and Credelio Quattro, and the largest customer is a distributor about 12 percent of FY2025 revenue (Q2 10-Q page:32; 10-K page:13). Risk mechanic: new-product volume supports revenue growth now, but a small number of distributors and five product families carry the base, so a destocking or competitive event transmits quickly to revenue and receivables. Credit implication: revenue visibility is good in the near term and concentrated in the medium term; monitor distributor inventory and new product share.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Elanco Animal Health Incorporated is a moderately leveraged but improving credit whose liquidity and maturity profile are adequate and whose main weakness is the quality and definition of its leverage. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,445 million at 2026-06-30 and required principal payments of only USD 63 million in each of 2026 and 2027, with no large maturity before 2028. The weakest point is that total debt including the finance lease is 3.91x trailing Adjusted EBITDA, against management's 3.1x net measure, while Adjusted EBITDA includes net add-backs of USD 236 million and claims outside the debt table sit beside it. What decides the outcome is whether trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,008 million converts to cash after restructuring, interest and a rising floating-rate exposure, and whether the USD 1,236 million falling due in 2028 is refinanced on similar terms.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, liquidity and the near maturity profile are strong relative to obligations. Elanco Animal Health Incorporated held cash of USD 530 million and about USD 915 million of undrawn facilities at 2026-06-30, a total of USD 1,445 million, which is 11.5 times the USD 126 million of required principal payments in 2026 and 2027 [CP-1]. No facility matures before June 2028, so liquidity is not a near-term constraint on this evidence.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Elanco Animal Health Incorporated has a diversified revenue base across pet health and farm animal products, about 200 brands and more than 90 countries, with Q2 2026 revenue up 10 percent reported and 8 percent in organic constant currency, driven by new products [CP-1; CP-1A]. Liquidity of USD 1,445 million and a light maturity schedule before 2028 provide time. Gross margin rose to 58.3 percent in Q2 2026 from 57.5 percent, and operating cash flow was USD 290 million in six months 2026 against USD 233 million, with net capital spending falling to USD 84 million from USD 122 million, so operating cash flow less net purchases was USD 379 million trailing [CP-1]. There is no sponsor, no dividend and no buyback beyond employee tax withholding, and the company repaid a net USD 563 million of borrowings in 2025 [CP-1A]. The October 2025 refinancing extended maturities. Covenant levels of 7.71 to 1.00 and 2.00 to 1.00 sit far from the proxies computed from the pack [CP-1].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Leverage remains high at 3.91x on total debt and 5.10x on reported EBITDA, the trailing reported result is a loss of USD 199 million, and tangible equity is negative at USD (1,461) million because goodwill and intangibles exceed total equity [CP-1]. Adjusted EBITDA relies on add-backs of USD 236 million, including cash restructuring. Claims outside the debt table, hedge roll-off, customer concentration (two distributors at about 19 percent of FY2025 revenue) and product concentration (five families at about 38 percent) add cash flow volatility, and the first half carries most of the parasiticide sales [CP-1; CP-1A]. The senior notes coupon of 4.900 percent has reset to 6.40 percent after earlier downgrades, which shows the cost of credit events [CP-1]. Governance documents, guarantor and collateral structure, achieved covenant ratios and ratings are missing, and the stated capital allocation flexibility at below 3x leverage is a monitoring point [CP-1A].

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against the cautious view is that Elanco generated operating cash flow of 290 in six months 2026 against 233, cut net capital spending to 84 from 122, took total debt including the lease from 4,045 to 3,944, holds 1,445 of liquidity, and has no facility maturing before June 2028. If trailing Adjusted EBITDA converts to cash as the first half suggests, deleveraging toward the management target of below 3x could come faster than the cautious view assumes. What would make that case win: third-quarter results with Adjusted EBITDA inside the 200 to 215 guided range, restructuring cash costs within the reserve of 86, and a refinancing of the 2028 maturities ahead of the August 2028 notes date. Downside chain with observable triggers: a distributor destocking or loss of Zenrelia share (first break: Pet Health volume, 718 in Q2) lowers Adjusted EBITDA; restructuring and acquisition payments continue regardless (transmission), drawing on cash of 530 and the undrawn revolver of about 750; unhedged floating-rate exposure of 1,489 raises interest; leverage drifts above 3.5x on the management measure ahead of the 1,236 due in 2028. Triggers to watch: quarterly Adjusted EBITDA against guidance, net leverage on the management measure, the revolver balance, any covenant certificate when obtainable, and hedge disclosures after August 2026.

Triggers to watch: quarterly Adjusted EBITDA against guidance, net leverage on the management measure, the revolver balance, any covenant certificate when obtainable, and hedge disclosures after August 2026.

### Readiness view

The effective source set supports the requested work with limitations. All four requested consumers are assessed as READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS; none is CONDITIONAL and none is BLOCKED. The audited annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases cover the periods the context names (Q2 2026 and FY2025), in the reporting currency, up to the latest evidence dated 2026-08-05, which is before the cutoff. The binding limitations are five. First, the newest balance sheet is at 2026-06-30, and no filing or release dated after 2026-08-05 is in the pack, so the Q3 2026 position is not supplied. Second, Adjusted EBITDA, net debt and the 3.1x net leverage ratio come only from management releases and exclude covenant adjustments; the filed 10-Qs print none of them. Third, no executed legal document is in the pack, so guarantors, security and covenant definitions rest on filing summaries and exhibit lists. Fourth, the reported covenant ratios are not printed, only the levels and compliance statements. Fifth, no fidelity review of the text extraction has been done, and the pack has no charts, images or slides. None of these blocks a consumer from starting, and each carries forward as a stated limit.

All seven sources identify Elanco Animal Health Incorporated as the registrant or the announcing company (page:1 of each). No source is draft, unsigned, blocked or a duplicate of another. The 10-K is audited; the 10-Qs are unaudited. The filed 10-K and 10-Qs control their own facts. The three releases are management claims and must not override the filings.

### Entity and perimeter

The registrant and reporting entity is Elanco Animal Health Incorporated and its subsidiaries, consolidated (10-K page:7; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:1). The company operates as a single reporting segment, so there is no segment profit measure other than consolidated net income (10-Q Q2 2026 page:24). The 10-K exhibit list names the roles in the debt: under the Credit Agreement dated 2020-08-01 as amended by Amendment No. 3 dated 2025-10-31, Elanco Animal Health Incorporated is borrower, Elanco US Inc. is co-borrower and Elanco Financing (Netherlands) B.V. is the Dutch borrower, with "subsidiary loan parties", JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent and U.S. and Canadian collateral agent, and Wilmington Trust, National Association as non-U.S. and non-Canadian collateral agent and security trustee (page:147). The 4.900 percent senior notes were issued by Elanco Animal Health Incorporated under an indenture with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas as trustee (page:146; page:111). The receivables facility is documented in a Receivables Loan Agreement among Elanco SPEAR LLC, Elanco US Inc., and the lenders and lender agents, with Coöperatieve Rabobank U.A., New York Branch named (page:146), and the receivables are pledged for it (page:110-111). The pack does not name the subsidiary loan parties, does not state whether the senior notes carry subsidiary guarantees, and does not list the collateral; the risk factors say only that a significant portion of assets is pledged under the credit facilities and call the notes "senior unsecured notes" (page:44). The issuer-versus-guarantor-versus-collateral map is therefore an unresolved gap, not a conclusion. The context names no borrower, parent or guarantor. The name in the context ("Inc") and the registrant name ("Incorporated") are the same entity.
### Period basis and version relationships

There is no perimeter recast in the pack. All periods are on one consolidated basis, with one change of scope: the AHV International B.V. acquisition closed on 2026-04-30 and its results are included since that date, with revenue described as not material in Q2 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:10-11, page:32). The aqua business was divested on 2024-07-09 (Feb release page:4), which affects FY2024 comparatives only. Quarter-versus-year-to-date labels are explicit in each report. The pack supports these discrete periods: Q3 2025 from the Q3 2025 10-Q (page:6), Q4 2025 from the February release (page:12), Q1 2026 from the May release (page:1) and Q2 2026 from the 10-Q and August release. Discrete Q3 2025 Adjusted EBITDA is not printed in any source (no Q3 2025 release is in the pack); it can be derived downstream and must be labelled derived.

Trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 1,008 as of 2026-06-30 is printed by the company (August release page:14). The pack also contains the components to rebuild it: FY2025 901 (February release page:18) plus six months 2026 of 622 less six months 2025 of 514 (August release page:14). The rebuilt figure is in Calculations.
### Debt and liquidity evidence present

Amounts in millions of USD at 2026-06-30 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:12): Term Loan B due 2032 1,095; Euro Term Loan due 2029 383 (original amount EUR 400 million, 10-K page:109); Incremental Term Facilities due 2028, 2029, 2031 and 2032 of 336, 170, 319 and 536; Revolving Credit Facility nil drawn on 750 of commitments, maturing July 2029; Securitization Facility 100 drawn, maturing June 2028; Senior Notes due 2028 750, bearing 6.40 percent; unamortized debt issuance costs (26); total debt 3,663; finance lease liability 255; total 3,918, of which 73 is current. Facility pricing, amortization and maturities are printed in the 10-K (page:109-111). The 10-K schedule of required principal payments at 2025-12-31 runs 2026 63, 2027 63, 2028 1,236, 2029 548, 2030 20, and 2031 and thereafter 1,860 (page:111); the 10-Q Q2 2026 gives no updated schedule.

Financial maintenance covenants under the Revolving Credit Facility are a net total leverage ratio not to exceed 7.71 to 1.00, without step-downs, and an interest coverage ratio of no less than 2.00 to 1.00, both on pro forma adjusted EBITDA for four quarters (10-K page:109; 10-Q Q3 2025 page:15). The Euro Term Loan has consistent covenants (10-K page:110). The Q2 2026 10-Q states compliance with all covenants at 2026-06-30 (page:12) but prints neither the levels nor the achieved ratios. The Senior Notes indenture limits liens and sale-leaseback transactions and restricts consolidation, merger or sale of substantially all assets (10-K page:111).

Liquidity inputs printed at 2026-06-30 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:36): cash and cash equivalents 530, unused Revolving Credit Facility capacity of approximately 750, and approximately 165 of undrawn Securitization Facility capacity that fluctuates with the borrowing base. At 2025-12-31 the comparable figures were 545, approximately 750 and approximately 120 (10-K page:82). No letters of credit drawn against the revolver are printed (searched, see Gaps). A significant part of cash is held outside the U.S. (page:36). Management's net debt at 2026-06-30 is 3,159 and net leverage 3.1 times trailing twelve month Adjusted EBITDA of 1,008, a management measure that excludes covenant-related adjustments (August release page:14).

Debt-like and other claims disclosed: liability for sale of future revenue to Blackstone of 315 at 2026-06-30 after a 295 payment received in May 2025, with an effective interest rate of 18.3 percent and imputed interest of 29 in six months 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:17); the corporate headquarters finance lease, with liability 255 and a purchase option and landlord put at 250 at the end of five years (10-K page:120-121); operating lease liabilities of 124 at 2025-12-31 (10-K page:121); AHV deferred cash consideration of 100 due through 2030, of which approximately 60 is payable in January 2027 and 20 in January 2028, and contingent consideration of up to 140 through 2032 carried at fair value 67 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:10); other contingent consideration of 19 for NutriQuest (page:16); a restructuring reserve of 86 (page:11-12); and pension and retirement obligations, with a funded status of (150) at 2025-12-31 (10-K page:133). Cash paid for interest was 206 and net cash taxes were 225 in FY2025 (10-K page:112, page:126). Six-month 2026 cash interest and cash taxes are not printed.
### Quarter, subsequent events and contingencies

Evidence present for the latest quarter and the period after it: the AHV acquisition closed on 2026-04-30 for total estimated consideration of 243, funded from cash on hand and a 50 draw on the Securitization Facility repaid within the quarter (page:10, page:30); the weighted-average effective interest rate on debt excluding the finance lease was 5.79 percent, with interest rate swaps of 2,300 notional maturing in August 2026 and forward-starting swaps of 1,450 effective August 2026 (page:14); the pack does not show what happened at those August 2026 dates; in July 2026 the company extended 200 million CHF of net investment hedges to 2031 (page:13); the Fourth Circuit appeal in the Barpar securities class action is pending after a dismissal with prejudice on 2026-03-26 (page:19); the Ninth Circuit affirmed the jury verdict in the Tevra matter on 2026-07-06 and denied rehearing on 2026-07-31 (page:22), with a settlement in principle of a non-material amount in two related class actions (page:22); the company states it has no material liabilities established for these legal matters (page:19). The 2026-08-05 release raised full-year revenue guidance to 5,090 to 5,140, Adjusted EBITDA to 1,010 to 1,035 and targeted a year-end net leverage ratio of approximately 3.0 times (August release page:1, page:4). That guidance is a management claim. No event dated after 2026-11-05 is relied on. The FY2026 guidance, the January 2027 and January 2028 deferred payments and the interest rate swap start dates are future dates stated as scheduled or expected, not as facts.

CP-1 (financial base) runs next, followed by CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Trailing Adjusted EBITDA of 1,008 against total debt of 3,944 including the finance lease gives 3.91x, versus management's 3.1x net measure. Liquidity of 1,445 and no large maturity before 2028 support the base. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure; trailing cash interest and achieved covenant ratios are not supplied; the latest balance sheet is June 30, 2026. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

### Financial base view

The financial base is usable for a credit snapshot, with the limits stated below. Elanco Animal Health Incorporated reports one consolidated perimeter and one segment, so every figure is group level. Revenue was 4,715 in FY2025 and 2,739 in the six months to 2026-06-30, up from 2,434 a year earlier; the trailing twelve month figure is 5,020. Reported net income was a loss of 232 in FY2025 because the fourth quarter carried 202 of impairment and restructuring charges; the trailing twelve month reported result is still a loss of 199, while six-month 2026 net income is 111. Adjusted EBITDA, which management defines and the filed statements do not print, was 901 in FY2025 and is printed as 1,008 for the trailing twelve months at 2026-06-30 (1,009 when rebuilt from the components, a rounding difference). Reported EBITDA from the same reconciliation is 773 on a trailing basis, so the net add-backs are 236.

Leverage depends on the definition. Management's net leverage, which deducts cash and the finance lease from gross debt, is 3.6x at 2025-12-31 and 3.1x at 2026-06-30. On a basis that keeps the 255 headquarters finance lease in debt and deducts only cash, net debt is 3,414 and net leverage 3.39x at 2026-06-30, and total debt leverage is 3.91x. On reported EBITDA, which still includes royalty revenue that is no longer received in cash, total debt leverage is 5.10x. Both bases are shown in the charts and the table because the choice moves the answer by nearly two turns between the lowest basis (3.13x, the company's) and the highest (5.10x, reported EBITDA).

Debt is bank term loans, a securitization facility and 750 of senior notes due 2028. Required principal payments are small until 2028, when 1,236 falls due, and 1,860 falls due in 2031 and later. Liquidity at 2026-06-30 is 530 of cash plus about 750 of undrawn revolver and about 165 of undrawn securitization capacity, 1,445 in total, and no facility matures before June 2028, when the securitization facility falls due. Operating cash flow was 290 in the six months, and operating cash flow less net purchases of property, equipment and software was 206. The main watch items are the dependence of Adjusted EBITDA on add-backs that include cash restructuring, the August 2026 roll-off of 2,300 of interest rate swaps, the debt-like claims outside the debt table (the 315 liability for sale of future revenue, the headquarters lease purchase option and acquisition payments) and the absence of any figure after 2026-08-05. Adjusted EBITDA, net leverage and guidance are management claims; the filed statements control every other figure.

### Adjusted EBITDA bridge and quality

Adjusted EBITDA starts from reported net income, adds net interest expense, income tax and depreciation and amortization to reach EBITDA, then adjusts for the cost of sales items, asset impairment, restructuring and other special charges, sold royalty revenue, the 2024 divestiture gain and other (income) expense items (Aug release page:14; Feb release page:18). For the trailing twelve months the adjustments are 252 of impairment, restructuring and other special charges, less 33 of sold royalty revenue, plus 16 of other expense items and 1 of cost of sales, in total 236, equal to 31 percent of reported EBITDA of 773 (calculation below). Three points matter for credit use. First, the sold royalty adjustment removes revenue that Elanco still books under GAAP but no longer receives in cash, because the XDEMVY royalties go to Blackstone through 2033-08-24 (Q2 10-Q page:17); removing it makes Adjusted EBITDA the more conservative measure on that item. Second, the special charges are not one-off in size or frequency: they were 127 in FY2023, 150 in FY2024, 237 in FY2025 and 252 trailing (10-K page:92; Q2 10-Q page:6). Third, the FY2025 charges include 155 of restructuring of which 116 is cash severance (Feb release page:3, page:5); the restructuring reserve stood at 124 at 2025-12-31 and 86 at 2026-06-30, with about 80 classified as current (Q2 10-Q page:11-12). That cash is spent after the add-back and does not appear in Adjusted EBITDA, though it is in operating cash flow.

Imputed interest of 33 in FY2025 and 29 in six months 2026 on the liability for sale of future revenue sits in reported interest expense but is excluded in the company's adjusted interest (Aug release page:3, page:12). It accretes the liability: the balance rose from 304 to 315 in six months because imputed interest of 29 exceeded royalty revenue applied of 18 (Q2 10-Q page:17).

| Incremental Term Facility due 2028 | 339 | 336 | Term SOFR plus 1.75% | 2028-08-12 | Quarterly installments |

| Unamortized debt issuance costs | (28) | (26) | Not applicable | Not applicable | Deducted in the balance sheet total of 3,762 and 3,663 |

The weighted-average effective interest rate on borrowings, after swaps and excluding the finance lease, was 5.76% at 2025-12-31 and 5.79% at 2026-06-30 (10-K page:113; Q2 10-Q page:14).
### Rate and hedge exposure

At 2026-06-30 floating-rate borrowings are the six term facilities (2,839) plus the securitization facility (100), 2,939 in total, against 750 of fixed-rate notes. Interest rate swaps of 2,300 notional convert floating to fixed and have scheduled maturities in August 2026; forward-starting swaps of 1,450 notional become effective in August 2026 with maturities between 2027 and 2031, up from 850 at 2025-12-31 (Q2 10-Q page:14). On the pack's figures the hedged floating debt falls from 2,300 to 1,450 after August 2026 and unhedged floating-rate borrowings rise from 639 to 1,489, before any hedging added after 2026-06-30, which the pack does not show. The company states that approximately 80 percent of borrowings were fixed or swapped at 2026-06-30 (page:12). The calculation below gives about 83 percent for the pre-August position and about 60 percent for the post-August position on the same base; the post-August figure is an analyst illustration, not a company statement. Net investment hedges (1,000 million CHF notional with tenors in 2026 and 2027, of which 200 million CHF was extended to 2031 in July 2026) generated 23 of interest income in six months 2026, recorded as a reduction of interest expense (page:13-14).
### Covenants

Two financial maintenance covenants apply under the Revolving Credit Facility and, on consistent terms, the Euro Term Loan: a net total leverage ratio of pro forma net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA not to exceed 7.71 to 1.00 for the preceding four quarters, not subject to step-downs, and an interest coverage ratio of pro forma adjusted EBITDA to cash interest expense of no less than 2.00 to 1.00 (10-K page:109-110; Q3-25 10-Q page:15). The company states compliance with all covenants at 2026-06-30 (Q2 10-Q page:12). The achieved ratios are not supplied. Both covenant definitions differ from the metrics here: they use pro forma figures and covenant adjustments that the company says reduce its net leverage ratio below the printed measure (Aug release page:14), and a different net debt and cash interest definition. As an illustration only, not a covenant calculation: net debt of 3,159 divided by 7.71 is about 410, so trailing Adjusted EBITDA of 1,008 could fall by about 59 percent before the leverage test is reached on those proxies; and twice FY2025 cash interest of 206 is 412, so Adjusted EBITDA of 901 could fall by about 54 percent before the cover test is reached. The Senior Notes indenture has no financial maintenance covenant in the pack; it limits liens and sale-leasebacks and restricts mergers and sales of substantially all assets (10-K page:111). The Securitization Facility has covenants on the composition of the receivables portfolio, with compliance stated at 2025-12-31 (page:111).
### Liquidity by facility

At 2026-06-30: cash and cash equivalents 530; revolver commitment 750, nothing drawn, unused capacity approximately 750; securitization facility drawn 100 with approximately 165 of undrawn capacity under a borrowing base (Q2 10-Q page:12, page:36). Total of these inputs is 1,445. No letters of credit or other usage of the revolver is printed in any source. The revolver matures in July 2029 and the securitization facility in June 2028, so no facility expires within twelve months of 2026-06-30. Known cash calls over the next twelve months that the pack supports: required amortization (63 for calendar 2026 and 63 for 2027 on the 2025-12-31 schedule), deferred AHV cash consideration of about 60 in January 2027, restructuring reserve payments (about 80 current), 2026 capital expenditure guided at 175 to 200 (10-K page:86), and interest. A fall in cash from 545 to 530 in six months came with 76 paid for the AHV acquisition, 89 of debt repayment and 35 of share withholding payments, against operating cash flow of 290.
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow was 560 in FY2025 and 290 in six months 2026 against 233 a year earlier. Quarterly operating cash flow was 13 in Q1 2026 and 277 in Q2 2026 (May release page:4; Aug release page:4), which shows the first-half seasonal pattern; the company notes that parasiticide sales concentrate in the first half (Q2 10-Q page:30). Working capital absorbed 239 in six months 2026 against 185, with receivables up from 873 to 1,077 and inventories up from 1,737 to 1,769 since 2025-12-31 (page:6-7). Net purchases of property, equipment and software fell to 84 from 122 on timing of the Elwood, Kansas monoclonal antibody plant spend (page:37). Cash taxes of 225 in FY2025 compare with a tax expense of 8, driven by payments on the 2024 aqua divestiture gain (10-K page:84, page:126-127), so FY2025 free cash flow is a poor guide to a normal tax year; six-month 2026 cash taxes are not supplied. Interest on the liability for sale of future revenue and the sold royalties are non-cash and sit in operating cash flow adjustments (Q2 10-Q page:7).

### Latest quarter and after

Q2 2026 revenue was 1,368, up 10 percent reported and 8 percent in organic constant currency, with Pet Health 718 and Farm Animal 633 (Q2 10-Q page:9; Aug release page:2). Gross margin was 58.3 percent against 57.5 percent (page:32). Net income was 54 and Adjusted EBITDA 288. The AHV International acquisition closed 2026-04-30 for total estimated consideration of 243, with 76 paid in cash and funded from cash on hand and a 50 draw on the securitization facility, repaid in the quarter (page:10, page:30). Net leverage as reported fell from 3.5x to 3.1x in the quarter (May release page:4; Aug release page:4). Management raised 2026 guidance to revenue of 5,090 to 5,140 and Adjusted EBITDA of 1,010 to 1,035 and targeted year-end net leverage of approximately 3.0x (Aug release page:1, page:4); these are management claims. Subsequent items in the 10-Q are the July 2026 extension of 200 million CHF of net investment hedges to 2031 (page:13) and legal: the Ninth Circuit affirmed the Tevra verdict on 2026-07-06 and denied rehearing on 2026-07-31 (page:22). No filing or release dated after 2026-08-05 is in the pack.
### Handoff consumption

This module opened the CP-0 handoff and used it as follows. It kept CP-0's finding that Adjusted EBITDA and net leverage come only from releases, and labels them as management measures throughout. It carried the covenant, guarantor and security gaps unchanged (see Gaps). It used FY2025 only for cash interest and cash taxes, as CP-0 advised, and derived Q3 2025 Adjusted EBITDA as 198 and labelled it derived. It refines one CP-0 statement: CP-0 recorded a difference of 2 between depreciation and amortization on the six-month 2026 cash flow statement (343) and in the EBITDA reconciliation (341) as not explained. The difference sits wholly in Q1 2026, where the cash flow statement shows 172 and the reconciliation 170 (Q1 10-Q page:7; May release page:14); Q2 2026 is 171 in both, because 343 less 172 is 171. The cause is still not given in the sources. The reconciliation figure is used inside the EBITDA bridge and the cash flow figure for cash analysis. CP-0 is otherwise not corrected.
### Definition risks

Adjusted EBITDA differs from reported EBITDA by sold royalty revenue, restructuring and impairment charges, other expense items and, in FY2024, the divestiture gain. The company's net debt deducts the finance lease as well as cash, which lowers its net leverage by about 0.3x against this module's net basis (3.1x against 3.39x at 2026-06-30). Covenant EBITDA and net debt are defined in the credit agreement, which is not supplied, and are not the same as either. The cash interest figure is net of cash interest received on net investment hedges, which flatters cover relative to gross interest paid.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Elanco is a diversified single-segment animal health company with no sponsor or controlling owner evidenced. The credit-relevant events are the 2025 refinancing, the Blackstone royalty sale, the headquarters lease and the 2026 AHV acquisition. | Medium | Beneficial ownership, executed financing documents and ratings are not in the pack; governance conclusions rest on documented actions only. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

### Business and transaction view

Elanco Animal Health Incorporated is a global animal health company selling pet health and farm animal products in more than 90 countries, with about 200 brands, as one reporting segment (10-K page:7-8; Q2 10-Q page:24, page:26). It was a Lilly business unit, became an independent company on 2018-09-18, completed separation from Lilly in March 2019 and bought Bayer Animal Health in August 2020 (10-K page:7). No sponsor, parent or controlling shareholder is evidenced in the pack, and the company says it does not anticipate paying dividends (10-K page:70). The creditor-relevant facts fall into three groups. First, the operating model is diversified by species and region but concentrated by channel and product: the largest customer was about 12 percent of FY2025 revenue and the top five product families about 38 percent, with seasonality in pet parasiticides that places most of Seresto and Advantage Family sales in the first half (10-K page:9, page:12-13). Second, the 2025 and 2026 transactions changed the capital structure: the October 2025 refinancing, the Blackstone sale of future royalties, the headquarters finance lease with a purchase option, and the AHV acquisition with deferred and contingent consideration. These are described in the Transaction summary and are priced in CP-1. Third, management is pursuing an innovation-led growth plan (Zenrelia, Credelio Quattro, Befrena) with a restructuring and a stated deleveraging path; those are management statements, and CP-1 shows that part of the improvement in leverage to date came from higher trailing Adjusted EBITDA rather than from repayment. Documented issuer behaviour is mainly supportive of creditors (debt repaid, no dividends, the AHV acquisition funded from cash on hand and a short-lived securitization draw), with two items that need monitoring: the use of a royalty monetization and a headquarters lease with a purchase option rather than debt, and management's statement that falling below 3x leverage will unlock capital allocation flexibility.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No new debt issue, sponsor transaction or change of control appears in the evidence after 2025-12-31. The relevant transactions are as follows. On 2025-10-31 Elanco refinanced the Term Loan B due 2027, paying off a balance of 2,102, with three new facilities of aggregate gross proceeds of 2,106 (the Term Loan B due 2032 of 1,100, the Euro Term Loan due 2029 of 400 million euros and the Incremental Term Facility due 2032 of 540) plus cash on hand; issuance costs and discounts were about 32 and 20 was charged to interest expense for refinancing costs and deferred cost write-offs (10-K page:75, page:109). The documented purpose was to extend the debt maturity profile and lower cash interest, which is a supportive action for creditors. In May 2025 Elanco sold to Blackstone the rights to U.S. royalties and sales milestones on XDEMVY owed by Tarsus for 295, with net proceeds of 290 used to repay debt; the rights run for U.S. net sales from 2025-04-01 to 2033-08-24, Elanco keeps ex-U.S. royalties and later U.S. royalties, and the liability is carried at 315 at 2026-06-30 with an effective interest rate of 18.3 percent (10-K page:75-76; Q2 10-Q page:17). That cost of capital is high against the term loans priced at Term SOFR plus 1.75 to 2.25 percent, and the pack does not say whether the royalty rights were part of the lenders' collateral. In June 2025 Elanco started a five-year finance lease on its new Indianapolis headquarters, with a purchase option and a landlord put at 250 at the end of the term, which management expects to exercise (10-K page:76, page:121); a City of Indianapolis tax increment incentive totalling 64 funds part of the project (page:121). In June 2025 the securitization facility was amended to extend its maturity to June 2028 (page:111). On 2026-02-19 Elanco signed to buy AHV International B.V., a Netherlands farm animal health company (10-K page:138, a subsequent event to that report), and closed on 2026-04-30 for total estimated purchase consideration of 243: 76 cash paid at closing, 100 of deferred cash due through 2030 and a contingent consideration fair value of 67 for up to 140 of milestone payments through 2032 (Q2 10-Q page:10). The acquisition was funded from cash on hand and a 50 draw on the securitization facility, drawn on 2026-04-22 and repaid in the quarter (Q1 10-Q page:11; Q2 10-Q page:30). Management says the deal does not materially affect the deleveraging timeline (Q2 10-Q page:30), a management statement. In 2024 Elanco sold its aqua business to Merck Animal Health for 1,294 in cash, used mostly to repay term loan debt (10-K page:105). Financing documents for these transactions are not in the pack and are known only through the descriptions cited. The Q4 2025 rating upgrade is described only through the senior notes rate reset from 6.650 to 6.40 percent (10-K page:111; Q2 10-Q page:12).

The pack evidences a widely held public company: 167 holders of record at 2026-02-19 and no stated controlling shareholder, sponsor or parent (10-K page:70). The pack describes no continuing Lilly shareholding; Lilly remains relevant through the tax matters agreement, under which pre-IPO tax liabilities remain with Lilly and the 2016 to 2018 U.S. examination is still ongoing (Q2 10-Q page:18). Equity-linked instruments were converted: 17.2 million shares were issued on conversion of tangible equity units in 2023 (10-K page:93). The 10-K lists activist shareholder action as a risk factor but names no activist (10-K page:6). Percentage ownership of any holder, board composition and control rights are not supplied: Item 12 on beneficial owners and the proxy statement are incorporated by reference and are not in the pack (10-K page:2). No percentage is inferred.

Evidence: Pet Health volume growth in Q2 2026 was driven by new products Zenrelia and Credelio Quattro, and the largest customer is a distributor about 12 percent of FY2025 revenue (Q2 10-Q page:32; 10-K page:13). Risk mechanic: new-product volume supports revenue growth now, but a small number of distributors and five product families carry the base, so a destocking or competitive event transmits quickly to revenue and receivables. Cash conversion and add-backs. Evidence: CP-1 shows trailing net add-backs of 236 to reported EBITDA, partly cash restructuring, and a restructuring reserve of 86 (Q2 10-Q page:11-12). ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Elanco is a moderately leveraged, improving credit with adequate liquidity and no large maturity before 2028. Its weak point is leverage quality: 3.91x on total debt, add-backs of USD 236 million and claims outside the debt table. | Medium | Executed debt documents, achieved covenant ratios, ratings and any evidence after 2026-08-05 are not in the pack. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Liquidity was USD 1,445 million at 2026-06-30 against required principal payments of USD 63 million in each of 2026 and 2027. | Near-term debt service and amortization are well covered. | High |

| Total debt including the finance lease fell from 4.49x to 3.91x trailing Adjusted EBITDA, mostly through higher earnings rather than repayment. | Deleveraging depends on earnings holding; the company's own net measure is 3.1x. | High |

| Adjusted EBITDA includes net add-backs of USD 236 million, and USD 1,236 million falls due in 2028 including the 750 senior notes. | Cash restructuring costs and the 2028 refinancing decide the outcome. | Medium |

| Claims outside the debt table include a USD 315 million royalty-sale liability at 18.3 percent, a USD 250 million headquarters option in 2030, and acquisition payments. | These calls on cash flow are not in the leverage ratio and their ranking against lenders is not shown. | Medium |

| Unhedged floating-rate debt rises from USD 639 million to USD 1,489 million after the August 2026 swap maturities, on the pack's figures. | Interest cost becomes more rate-sensitive, about USD 15 million a year per 100 basis points. | Medium |
### Credit view

Elanco Animal Health Incorporated is a moderately leveraged but improving credit whose liquidity and maturity profile are adequate and whose main weakness is the quality and definition of its leverage. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,445 million at 2026-06-30 and required principal payments of only USD 63 million in each of 2026 and 2027, with no large maturity before 2028. The weakest point is that total debt including the finance lease is 3.91x trailing Adjusted EBITDA, against management's 3.1x net measure, while Adjusted EBITDA includes net add-backs of USD 236 million and claims outside the debt table sit beside it. What decides the outcome is whether trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,008 million converts to cash after restructuring, interest and a rising floating-rate exposure, and whether the USD 1,236 million falling due in 2028 is refinanced on similar terms.
### Credit assessment
| Dimension | View | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Business risk | Diversified by species, region and about 200 brands, with growth led by new products; concentrated by distributor (about 12 percent and 7 percent of FY2025 revenue) and by five product families (about 38 percent), and seasonal in the first half | Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation | High | Business and transaction context, operating model; financial base, revenue |

| Financial risk | Leverage 3.91x total debt and 3.39x net debt including the finance lease on trailing Adjusted EBITDA; 5.10x on reported EBITDA; reported net loss of USD 199 million over the trailing twelve months; goodwill and intangibles of USD 8,049 million exceed equity of USD 6,588 million | Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Financial base, leverage and metrics tables |

| Liquidity | USD 530 million of cash plus about USD 750 million undrawn revolver and about USD 165 million undrawn securitization capacity, no facility maturing before June 2028; part of cash is held outside the U.S. | Documentary Fact | High | Financial base, liquidity chart |

| Refinancing | USD 63 million due in each of 2026 and 2027, USD 1,236 million in 2028, USD 548 million in 2029, USD 20 million in 2030 and USD 1,860 million from 2031; the 4.900 percent senior notes now bear 6.40 percent | Documentary Fact | High | Financial base, maturity chart and debt terms |

| Creditor control and governance | No sponsor or controlling holder evidenced; no dividends; covenants at 7.71 to 1.00 net leverage and 2.00 to 1.00 interest cover with compliance stated; guarantors, collateral and baskets not supplied | Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information | Medium | Financial base, covenants; business and transaction context, governance |
| Information quality | Latest evidence is 2026-08-05; Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure; no ratings | Insufficient Information | Medium | Readiness handoff |
### Key findings

First, liquidity and the near maturity profile are strong relative to obligations. Elanco Animal Health Incorporated held cash of USD 530 million and about USD 915 million of undrawn facilities at 2026-06-30, a total of USD 1,445 million, which is 11.5 times the USD 126 million of required principal payments in 2026 and 2027 [CP-1]. No facility matures before June 2028, so liquidity is not a near-term constraint on this evidence.

Second, leverage has improved but its level depends on the definition. Total debt including the finance lease fell from 4.49x trailing Adjusted EBITDA at 2025-12-31 to 3.91x at 2026-06-30 and net leverage on the company's definition fell from 3.6x to 3.1x [CP-1]. Most of the improvement came from higher Adjusted EBITDA rather than repayment: debt fell by USD 101 million while trailing Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 901 million to USD 1,008 million [CP-1]. On reported EBITDA the same total debt is 5.10x.

Third, the quality of Adjusted EBITDA is the main analytical risk. Net add-backs of USD 236 million equal 31 percent of reported trailing EBITDA of USD 773 million, special charges have run at USD 127 million, USD 150 million, USD 237 million and USD 252 million in FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 and the trailing twelve months, and part of the restructuring is cash with a reserve of USD 86 million still to be paid [CP-1]. The removal of sold royalty revenue works in the other direction and makes the measure more conservative on that item [CP-1].

Fourth, important claims sit outside the leverage ratio. The liability for sale of future revenue to Blackstone is USD 315 million with an effective interest rate of 18.3 percent, the headquarters finance lease has a USD 250 million purchase option or landlord put in 2030 that management expects to exercise, the AHV acquisition carries USD 100 million of deferred cash and up to USD 140 million of contingent payments, and pension funded status is USD (150) million [CP-1; CP-1A]. The pack does not show how these rank against lenders or whether the royalty rights were collateral.

Fifth, 2028 is the refinancing event. USD 1,236 million of required principal falls due in 2028, which is 33 percent of the scheduled total and includes the USD 750 million senior notes due 2028-08-28, an incremental term facility due 2028-08-12 and the securitization facility due June 2028 [CP-1]. The company refinanced its 2027 term loan in October 2025 into facilities maturing in 2029 and 2032, which shows market access, and management targets net leverage below 3x in 2027 [CP-1A].

Sixth, interest sensitivity is rising. Interest rate swaps of USD 2,300 million notional mature in August 2026 against forward-starting swaps of USD 1,450 million, so unhedged floating-rate debt rises from USD 639 million to USD 1,489 million on the pack's figures, about USD 15 million a year for each 100 basis points before any later hedging that the pack does not show [CP-1]. Fiscal year 2025 cash interest cover on Adjusted EBITDA was 4.37x, or 3.62x before interest received on net investment hedges [CP-1]; trailing cash interest is not supplied.

Seventh, the information base limits confidence. Covenant levels are printed but achieved ratios are not, the credit agreement, indenture, guarantor list and collateral are not supplied, there are no ratings, and nothing after 2026-08-05 is in the pack [CP-0; CP-1]. On the proxies in the financial base, trailing Adjusted EBITDA could fall by about 59 percent before the leverage covenant level is reached and by about 54 percent before the interest cover level is reached, but covenant definitions differ and these are not headroom.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Elanco Animal Health Incorporated has a diversified revenue base across pet health and farm animal products, about 200 brands and more than 90 countries, with Q2 2026 revenue up 10 percent reported and 8 percent in organic constant currency, driven by new products [CP-1; CP-1A]. Liquidity of USD 1,445 million and a light maturity schedule before 2028 provide time. Gross margin rose to 58.3 percent in Q2 2026 from 57.5 percent, and operating cash flow was USD 290 million in six months 2026 against USD 233 million, with net capital spending falling to USD 84 million from USD 122 million, so operating cash flow less net purchases was USD 379 million trailing [CP-1]. There is no sponsor, no dividend and no buyback beyond employee tax withholding, and the company repaid a net USD 563 million of borrowings in 2025 [CP-1A]. The October 2025 refinancing extended maturities. Covenant levels of 7.71 to 1.00 and 2.00 to 1.00 sit far from the proxies computed from the pack [CP-1].

Weaknesses. Leverage remains high at 3.91x on total debt and 5.10x on reported EBITDA, the trailing reported result is a loss of USD 199 million, and tangible equity is negative at USD (1,461) million because goodwill and intangibles exceed total equity [CP-1]. Adjusted EBITDA relies on add-backs of USD 236 million, including cash restructuring. Claims outside the debt table, hedge roll-off, customer concentration (two distributors at about 19 percent of FY2025 revenue) and product concentration (five families at about 38 percent) add cash flow volatility, and the first half carries most of the parasiticide sales [CP-1; CP-1A]. The senior notes coupon of 4.900 percent has reset to 6.40 percent after earlier downgrades, which shows the cost of credit events [CP-1]. Governance documents, guarantor and collateral structure, achieved covenant ratios and ratings are missing, and the stated capital allocation flexibility at below 3x leverage is a monitoring point [CP-1A].
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| Leverage definition and add-back quality | Reported EBITDA of USD 773 million trailing is below Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,008 million; restructuring cash is paid after the add-back | Leverage on Adjusted EBITDA overstates cash capacity; test cash flow alongside | Material | Financial base, EBITDA bridge |

| 2028 refinancing | USD 1,236 million due in 2028 including USD 750 million senior notes bearing 6.40 percent | Market access and earnings at that time decide the cost; failure would draw on liquidity of USD 1,445 million | Material | Financial base, maturity chart |

| Claims outside the debt table | Royalty-sale liability, headquarters option, AHV payments, pensions and reserve call on cash through 2033 | Debt service coverage should include them; ranking unknown | Material | Financial base, claims table; business context, transactions |

| Customer, product and seasonal concentration | Two distributors and five product families carry the base, with most parasiticide sales in the first half | A destocking or competitive event moves revenue, receivables and cash flow quickly | Material | Business context, operating model |

| Execution of growth and cost programmes | Growth rests on Zenrelia, Credelio Quattro and Befrena launches and restructuring savings that management targets | Missed launches would slow deleveraging; targets are management claims | Material | Business context, governance |

| Information gaps | Documents, covenant achieved ratios, ratings, guarantors and post-quarter data are not supplied | Priority of claims and covenant headroom cannot be assessed | Material | Readiness handoff |

| Floating-rate exposure | Swaps fall from USD 2,300 million to USD 1,450 million in August 2026 | About USD 15 million a year per 100 basis points, small against trailing operating cash flow of USD 617 million | Minor | Financial base, hedge exposure |

| Litigation and regulation | Securities appeal, Tevra and related class actions, antibiotic regulation (9 percent shared-class and 15 percent animal-only antibiotic revenue) | No material liabilities established; remains open | Minor | Business context, operating model |
## Calculations
New calculations in this module, in USD millions; all inputs are from the upstream handoffs and were spot checked to the sources named in brackets.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The figures, locators and derived ratios in the financial base, business context and synthesis trace to the filings and recompute correctly, and the three agree. Committee use is restricted by missing documents, covenant ratios and ratings, not by tracing failures. | Medium | The review was done in the same session as the analysis and from the same extraction text, so it is not independent. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

### Evidence trace view

The evidence trace holds. Each material claim in the financial base, business context and credit synthesis handoffs was matched to a located source span or to a recomputation from located figures, and the three handoffs agree on every shared figure, period and perimeter label. The synthesis view, a moderately leveraged and improving credit with Medium confidence, follows from the cited basis and is not overstated. Four statements are only partly supported, all as wording rather than figures. No claim is unsupported and no contradiction between modules was found. The integrity verdict for the evaluated set is Restricted, not Committee Ready, because the conclusions that matter most to a creditor, namely covenant headroom, structural priority, ratings and the position after 2026-08-05, rest on documents and data that are not in the sources. The review is limited: it was done in the same session as the analysis, from the same extraction text, and the page locators are extraction chunks rather than printed pages.

### Cross-module contradictions

None found. Pairs examined and found consistent: strong liquidity in CP-2 against a trailing reported loss and negative tangible equity in CP-1; improving leverage in CP-2 against dependence on add-backs in CP-1; no dividends or buybacks in CP-1A against employee tax withholding purchases of 35, which CP-1A discloses; management's deleveraging target in CP-1A (Management Language) against the leverage bases in CP-1; the 3.1x management measure against the 3.91x total-debt measure, which differ by the finance lease and covenant adjustments, both stated.
### Verdict consistency

The verdicts agree across modules for every shared claim. CP-2's Medium confidence is no higher than the readiness judgment of CP-1A (ready with limitations) allows, and its gap list matches the inherited gaps. CP-2 contains no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the cautious view is that Elanco generated operating cash flow of 290 in six months 2026 against 233, cut net capital spending to 84 from 122, took total debt including the lease from 4,045 to 3,944, holds 1,445 of liquidity, and has no facility maturing before June 2028. If trailing Adjusted EBITDA converts to cash as the first half suggests, deleveraging toward the management target of below 3x could come faster than the cautious view assumes. What would make that case win: third-quarter results with Adjusted EBITDA inside the 200 to 215 guided range, restructuring cash costs within the reserve of 86, and a refinancing of the 2028 maturities ahead of the August 2028 notes date. Downside chain with observable triggers: a distributor destocking or loss of Zenrelia share (first break: Pet Health volume, 718 in Q2) lowers Adjusted EBITDA; restructuring and acquisition payments continue regardless (transmission), drawing on cash of 530 and the undrawn revolver of about 750; unhedged floating-rate exposure of 1,489 raises interest; leverage drifts above 3.5x on the management measure ahead of the 1,236 due in 2028. Triggers to watch: quarterly Adjusted EBITDA against guidance, net leverage on the management measure, the revolver balance, any covenant certificate when obtainable, and hedge disclosures after August 2026.
